hook_text: How did one region of south-eastern Europe help to start a world war?
clip_script: By 1914, Europe was packed with explosives. Militarism: millions of conscripts and a race to build battleships like HMS Dreadnought. Alliances: Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy on one side; Britain, France and Russia on the other. Imperialism: quarrels over colonies, from Morocco to Africa. Nationalism: French anger over Alsace and Lorraine, and Serbs wanting their own nation. The Balkans were the powder keg. All it needed was a spark. Remember M, A, I, N.
visual_style: A whiteboard map of Europe in 1914 with two coloured alliance blocs, battleship and soldier icons, and a fuse burning toward the Balkans.
pacing: Builds cause by cause to the spark.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to master the causes of the First World War.
